subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: 'Smocking' is a technique that...
options: Gathers fabric with stitches to create decorative texture and stretch
questions.explain: Smocking gathers and stitches fabric to make a flexible, decoratively textured surface.

questions.q: 'Leading' in typography refers to the...
questions.explain: Leading is the vertical spacing between lines of type, affecting readability.

questions.q: Which natural fibre comes from the cocoon of the silkworm?
questions.explain: Silk is a natural protein fibre produced by silkworms when they spin their cocoons.

questions.q: Which printmaking process is described as 'intaglio', where ink is held in lines cut below the surface?
questions.explain: Etching is an intaglio process: ink sits in the recessed bitten lines, not on the raised surface.

questions.q: Weaving creates fabric by...
options: Interlacing warp and weft threads at right angles
Looping a single yarn with needles
questions.explain: Weaving interlaces vertical warp threads with horizontal weft threads to make cloth.

questions.q: 'Architecture' is a branch of design concerned with...
questions.explain: Architecture is the design of buildings and the spaces people use.

questions.q: What is 'stippling'?
options: Building tone using many small dots
questions.explain: Stippling builds up tone and texture using numerous small dots placed close together.

questions.q: In 3D design, 'structure' refers to...
options: How a form is built and held together to stay stable
questions.explain: Structure concerns how a 3D object is constructed and supported so it stands and holds together.

questions.q: The CMYK colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, key/black) is the standard ink set used in colour printing.

questions.q: A 'design brief' usually sets out...
options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.

questions.q: What is tie-dye?
options: Binding fabric tightly before dyeing so bound areas resist the dye
questions.explain: In tie-dye, fabric is tied or bound so the bound parts resist the dye, creating patterns.

questions.q: A 'vector' image is one that...
options: Is made of pixels and blurs when enlarged
Can only be black and white
Uses mathematical paths so it scales without losing quality
questions.explain: Vector graphics use mathematical paths, so they can be scaled to any size without pixelation.

questions.q: Batik is a textile technique that uses what to resist dye?
questions.explain: In batik, hot wax is applied to fabric so the waxed areas resist the dye.

questions.q: Which material is shaped while soft and then fired hard in a kiln?
questions.explain: Clay is modelled while soft, then fired in a kiln to become hard and permanent.

questions.q: Joining materials together to make a 3D form is called...
questions.explain: Construction (or assembly) builds a 3D form by joining separate pieces together.

questions.q: What does adding black to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding black to a colour produces a shade (a darker version), whereas adding white produces a tint.

questions.q: Expressionism aims above all to convey...
options: The artist's inner emotion and feeling
questions.explain: Expressionism distorts colour and form to express the artist's emotional response rather than reality.

questions.q: Lino printing is an example of which type of printmaking?
questions.explain: In relief printing such as lino, ink sits on the raised surface while cut-away areas stay blank.

questions.q: What is 'typography' in graphic design?
options: The art of arranging type and lettering
questions.explain: Typography is the design and arrangement of type so that text is legible and appealing.

questions.q: What is 'pattern' as a formal element?
options: The edge that defines a shape
A repeated arrangement of shapes, lines or colours
The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Pattern is created when elements such as shapes or marks are repeated in an organised way.

questions.q: Bonding (interfacing) fabric with heat from an iron usually relies on...
options: A glue web or adhesive that melts
questions.explain: Bondaweb and fusible interfacing carry a heat-activated adhesive that melts to join fabrics.

questions.q: Felting makes fabric by...
options: Matting and pressing fibres together with moisture and friction
questions.explain: Felting binds loose fibres into a fabric by pressing them with moisture, heat and friction.
